name: Binnui
overview: Binnui is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Bani who had married a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:38. No tribal affiliation or additional personal details are provided in Scripture. His mention highlights a specific genealogical and covenantal concern within the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Binnui is a proper name meaning "son." There is no indication that this name was given by God, and it appears only once in Scripture in Ezra 10:38 without further elaboration on its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Binnui as a descendant of Bani, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented for Binnui in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Binnui's significance lies in his identification as a descendant of Bani who had taken a foreign wife, a matter addressed in Ezra 10 during the post-exilic reforms. This highlights the community's efforts to maintain covenant purity by addressing intermarriage with foreign peoples. His mention serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by God's people in preserving their identity and faithfulness after the exile.
